Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexWave Communications Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, participants are required to utilize handset microphones for optimal sound quality. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NexWave Communications' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Chris Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Dana Patel, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Chris Harlan: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We achieved robust subscriber growth with total net additions exceeding expectations, reflecting our strong execution in a dynamic market. We are particularly excited about the initial performance of our WaveStream service and its positive impact on bundling and engagement across our customer base. Our investments in fiber buildout are also paying off, driving increased coverage, adoption, and customer satisfaction. Furthermore, we have focused on churn reduction through network superiority and retention initiatives, which has allowed us to maintain industry-leading loyalty. Finally, our strategic emphasis on operating expense discipline continues to enhance profitability and position us for accelerated growth.

Dana Patel: Thank you, Chris. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $15.0 billion, representing a 3.8% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $5.7 billion, with a margin of 38%. We continue to manage our expenses effectively and are on track to meet our financial targets for the year. Our capital expenditures were $2.6 billion, primarily driven by investments in our 5G network expansion.

To give you more context on our operating expense management initiatives and their impact on profitability, let me highlight the key areas where we've driven efficiency. In Q3, we delivered adjusted OpEx of $2.42 billion, down 7% year-over-year and 3% sequentially from Q2. This represents $185 million in sequential savings and a cumulative $650 million in run-rate OpEx reductions since the start of 2023. These efforts directly contributed to our adjusted EBITDA of $1.85 billion on a segment basis, up 12% year-over-year, expanding our EBITDA margin by 320 basis points to 38.2%—our highest in five years and ahead of peers like Comcast and Verizon.

Breaking it down, our largest bucket is network operations and infrastructure optimization, delivering $280 million in annualized savings. Our telecom backbone accounts for 42% of total OpEx, or about $1.02 billion in Q3. We've accelerated the shift to cloud-native architectures and network function virtualization, reducing legacy TDM and proprietary hardware costs. Specifically, migrating 65% of our core network to our Open RAN platform, partnered with Nokia and Rakuten Symphony, cut energy and maintenance expenses by 18% year-over-year. Predictive analytics powered by our AI-driven OSS platform prevented $45 million in unplanned outages through machine learning-based fault prediction, slashing mean time to repair by 40%.

Regionally, North America benefited most with $120 million in savings from densifying our 5G Standalone footprint in high-ARPU markets like the Northeast Corridor, where we've reclaimed 15% spectrum efficiency via dynamic spectrum sharing. In Europe, despite regulatory headwinds from the EU's Gigabit Society mandate, we captured $60 million by consolidating 200 edge sites amid our Vodafone UK joint venture unwind. In APAC, particularly India through our partnership similar to Airtel, we delivered $100 million through low-cost small-cell deployments, offsetting inflation in tower leases.

Next, content and media rights efficiency generated $210 million in annualized savings. Media OpEx, at 28% of total or $678 million, faced pressure from the streaming wars, with linear TV cord-cutting accelerating to 4.2% quarterly churn. We renegotiated 75% of our content portfolio, prioritizing first-window sports rights like NFL Sunday Ticket analogs and bundling with our WaveStream SVOD service. This reduced acquisition costs per hour by 22%, saving $90 million in Q3 alone. We've implemented a content recommendation engine using AWS SageMaker, boosting viewer retention by 15% and amortizing rights over longer useful lives—from 18 to 24 months on average. We also sunsetted 12 underperforming linear channels, redirecting $50 million to FAST channels, mirroring Roku and Pluto TV's model. In Latin America, where telenovela rights are hyper-competitive, we localized 40% of content via AI dubbing, yielding $40 million in savings while growing monthly active users 25% year-over-year.

SG&A and overhead rationalization added $160 million in annualized savings. SG&A came in at $722 million, down 12% year-over-year, driven by zero-based budgeting and a 9% headcount reduction to 48,000 full-time equivalents, focused on non-customer-facing roles. Our Workday HCM platform automated 70% of procurement and vendor management, capturing $75 million via AI-sourced supplier auctions. Marketing spend optimized to $280 million, with a 25% shift to performance-based digital channels like CTV and DOOH, improving customer acquisition cost by 16% to $320 per broadband sub, while preserving our 92% postpaid wireless retention.

These initiatives are embedded in our Efficiency 2.0 framework, targeting $1 billion in OpEx leverage for the full year. The $650 million year-to-date savings directly boosted free cash flow to $1.2 billion in Q3—up 22% year-over-year—and deleveraged our net debt to EBITDA to 2.4 times from 3.1 times last year. Margins now rival T-Mobile's leading 40% levels, positioning us for 5-7% free cash flow yield. Strategically, in telecom we're front-running 6G R&D with Ericsson, using savings to fund $800 million in mid-band spectrum auctions next year. In media, amid Netflix and Disney+ price hikes, our bundled 5G-home broadband-WaveStream offering lifted blended ARPU 4% to $68, with 85% take rates. Risks include FX volatility in emerging markets and potential ultra-low access fees regulation in Europe, but our 60/40 telecom-media mix hedges this. For Q4, we guide OpEx to $2.35 to $2.40 billion, implying another $100 million in sequential savings, with full-year EBITDA growth of 14-16%. This discipline funds our $15 billion capex plan—40% growth-focused—while returning $2.5 billion to shareholders via buybacks and our 2.8% yield.

Shifting to churn rate analysis, trends and drivers, this remains a critical leading indicator for subscriber retention and long-term revenue stability across our telecom and media segments. Churn, defined as the percentage of subscribers who disconnect or downgrade within a given period, directly impacts our monthly recurring revenue, ARPU, and net adds. Our blended churn rate across wireless, broadband, and streaming improved to 1.12% quarterly in Q3, down 15 basis points year-over-year from 1.27%, and our best quarterly result since Q1 2022. This equates to a 12% year-over-year reduction in absolute churn dollars, retaining an additional 450,000 subscribers and shielding about $180 million in annualized revenue.

Postpaid wireless churn dipped to a post-pandemic low of 0.82%, versus 1.05% year-over-year, outperforming the industry average of 0.95% per New Street Research. Family plan churn held at 0.65%, supported by Unlimited Plus bundles. Prepaid wireless improved to 3.45% monthly from 3.85% year-over-year, though elevated in price-sensitive segments. Broadband and fiber churn was a standout at 1.05% quarterly versus 1.35% year-over-year, thanks to FTTH deployments. Streaming and media churn stabilized at 4.2% monthly versus 5.1% year-over-year, competitive with Netflix's 4.0% global average and better than Disney+ Bundle's 4.8% in the U.S.

Our churn trajectory shows a clear downtrend since the Q4 2023 peak of 1.45%, with four consecutive quarters of sequential improvement, ahead of Comcast's 1.28% video/broadband blended and Verizon's 0.92% postpaid.

Positive drivers include network superiority—our 5G Ultra Wideband coverage at 85% of top 100 U.S. markets correlated to 22% lower churn in covered areas versus 4G, with standalone 5G at just 0.68% versus 1.12% for 4G-only. Our content ecosystem, with Peacock-like live sports bundling, reduced media churn by 18%, and in NexWave Stream plus Mobile bundle markets, it fell 25% year-over-year. Economic resilience limited voluntary downgrades to 8% of churn despite inflation.

Challenges came from competitive intensity, with T-Mobile's Go5G promos and AT&T fiber overbuilds driving 35% of wireless losses, especially in the Midwest. Cord-cutting spiked video churn 10% quarter-over-quarter in rural areas due to vMVPDs like YouTube TV and Hulu + Live, aligning with 22 million U.S. households cutting pay-TV last year per eMarketer. Macro pressures raised economic churn to 28% of total from 20% year-over-year, hitting prepaid and low-income broadband. Service disruptions from weather added 5-7 basis points, though mean-time-to-repair improved 15% via AI field ops.

Regionally, North America, 65% of subs, led at 0.95% blended, with U.S. postpaid at 0.78% beating Verizon's 0.85%; Canada ticked up to 1.05% from consolidation spillover. Europe, 18% of subs, was higher at 1.45% due to roaming caps and UK merger scrutiny at 2.1%, though Spain and Italy improved with low-cost 5G. APAC and LATAM, 17% of subs, hit 1.68%, with Brazil prepaid at 4.2% monthly amid devaluation and competition; India stabilized at 3.1% post-Jio hikes thanks to our Viacom18 JV.

Our AI-powered churn prediction engine, live on 90% of the base using 200+ variables like usage and NPS, flags at-risk subs 30 days early, lifting save rates 28% and averting $120 million in Q3 losses. Dynamic pricing micro-segmentation offers personalized credits, cutting high-value churn 35%. Bundling 2.0 with Total Home packages yields 2.5 times lower churn at 0.72% than single-play. Enterprise fixed wireless is sub-0.5%, targeting Starlink with SLAs. Content investments of $500 million aim for under 4% streaming churn by FY25. We guide blended churn to 1.05-1.10% for Q4, with wireless toward 0.75%, supporting 2.2 million FY24 net adds and 3-4% revenue growth. Our retention flywheel—networks, content, data-driven saves—is de-risking 15% EBITDA margins.

Now, on fiber buildout progress, coverage expansion, and customer adoption, as we execute our multi-year transformation into a fiber-first powerhouse, this is the cornerstone against cable peers like Comcast and Charter, complementing wireless and countering fixed wireless from T-Mobile and Verizon. In Q3, we deployed an additional 4,200 route miles of fiber—up 15% quarter-over-quarter—for year-to-date 12,800 miles, on track for 17,000 miles full-year, a 25% increase from 2023. Construction productivity improved with splicing teams at 1,200 feet per day per crew, partnerships with Dycom and MasTec, drone surveys, and AI permitting shaving 20% off timelines. Capex for fiber was $450 million this quarter, 60% property and equipment, 40% engineering and outside plant.

Coverage expanded with 1.2 million new homes passed to a record 18.4 million nationwide—a 28% year-over-year increase. This spans cluster builds in metros and extensions in suburbs. In the Southeast, our strongest market, 450,000 new homes pushed penetration to 35% in Atlanta and Charlotte MSAs, aided by $120 million YTD RDOF Phase I. Midwest added 350,000 with Indianapolis and Kansas City at 90% completion, prioritizing XGS-PON for 10G symmetric speeds ahead of AT&T. California and Texas clusters added 250,000 despite permitting delays from wildfires and zoning—still 20% ahead via micro-trenching. Rural BEAD projects added 150,000 homes passed, with $850 million provisional awards across 12 states for middle-mile.

Our addressable footprint covers 62% of top 40 markets, up from 48% a year ago, with engineering for another 2.5 million into Q4.

Customer adoption hit an inflection, with fiber broadband subscribers up 285,000 in Q3—our best ever—to 4.2 million total RGUs, a 42% year-over-year surge. Sequential adds compounded at 22% since Q1, take rates at 22.8% on homes passed in mature clusters, up 300 basis points, exceeding 35% in 18-month-old clusters like top Frontier markets.

Drivers: aggressive 1Gig pricing at $70/month with Disney Bundle at 65% attach, boosting ARPU to $118—up 8%—and video RGUs 12% with 200+ channels plus FAST. Low churn at 0.85% monthly versus 1.4% DOCSIS average, via speed migrations—80% new subs on 2Gig+. Sales converted 28% from door-to-door and digital, self-install cutting CAC 15% to $650.

We've activated 10G PON on 1,200 nodes for 40% take rates in upgrades, piloting Open RAN for hybrid fiber-wireless. ROI shows payback at 28 months from 36, L2/L3 improving with scale. 55% of 2025 capex—$2.2 billion—to fiber, targeting 25 million homes passed by YE26 and 8 million subs, harvesting $1.5 billion incremental EBITDA by 2027 despite supply pressures on Nokia and Adtran OLTs. This fiber engine delivers 15-20% broadband revenue growth.

I'll now turn to our outlook for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2025, expecting continued momentum across our integrated telecom and media ecosystem. As a reminder, NexWave operates as a converged player with over 145 million wireless connections, 28 million fixed broadband households, and 22 million streaming subscribers via WaveStream—positioning us uniquely against pure-play telcos like AT&T or Verizon, and streamers like Netflix and Disney.

On subscriber growth, we're guiding to total net additions of 1.2 to 1.5 million across segments in Q4, bringing full-year FY2025 net adds to 5.5 to 6.0 million—a 4% year-over-year increase from FY2024's 5.3 million. Wireless postpaid net adds: 750,000 to 900,000 in Q4, up from 680,000 in Q3, driven by 5G Ultra Wideband at 95% population coverage by year-end. FY2025 guidance is 3.8 to 4.2 million postpaid adds, about 2.7% growth to 142 million subs. This reflects premium segment share gains, ARPU steady at $55.20 in Q3 via Apple iPhone 16 uptake at 25% of new subs and Samsung financing. Churn at best-in-class 0.78%, below industry per New Street.

Fixed broadband net adds: 300,000 to 400,000 in Q4 from Q3's 280,000, FY2025 at 1.4 to 1.6 million—a 12% trajectory to 30 million households. FTTH passes 55 million locations, up 20%, take rates 55% in new builds, fueled by $3.2 billion BEAD awards across 12 states for gigabit symmetrical competing with Comcast Xfinity.

WaveStream video net adds: 150,000 to 200,000 in Q4 versus 120,000 in Q3, FY2025 800,000 to 1.0 million for 4% growth to 23 million subs. Amid 5% pay-TV household drop per Nielsen, bundled 5G/WaveStream drove 30% adds, penetration 16% of postpaid. NFL Sunday Ticket exclusives and NexAI personalization yield 25% higher engagement, 15% lower churn at 4.2%.

U.S. operations, 85% of subs, drive 80% adds; EMEA 15% growth from 5G SA in UK/Germany; APAC 50,000 from India JV.

Revenue-wise, raising outlook: Q4 total service revenue $14.6 to $14.8 billion, up 4.2% to 5.5% from $14.0 billion, total revenue $15.1 to $15.3 billion, plus 3.8% to 5.2%. Embeds 150 basis points pricing from 2-3% hikes on 5G Unlimited.

FY2025 service revenue $58.0 to $58.8 billion, 4.0% to 5.3% organic over $55.8 billion—ahead of 3.8% consensus. Total $60.5 to $61.3 billion, plus 4.1% to 5.8%. Wireless Q4 service 9.8 to 9.9 billion, plus 4.5-5.3%, FY 39.5-40.0 billion, plus 4.2-5.0%. Fixed broadband Q4 2.9-3.0 billion, plus 7.0-8.5%, FY 11.8-12.1 billion, plus 9.5-11.0%. WaveStream and media Q4 1.3-1.35 billion, plus 5.5-7.5%, FY 5.3-5.5 billion, plus 6.0-7.8%. Enterprise and other Q4 0.6 billion plus 2.0%, FY 1.4 billion plus 3.0%.

Wireless anchored by 2.5% ARPU from premium 5G and FWA to 2 million subs. Broadband from 8% residential penetration uplift in fiber and AWS dark fiber. Media per sub to $12.50 via ad-tiers at 35% new subs and linear migrations like Disney bundles.

Assumes normalized handset sales post-iPhone, no spectrum impacts—we hold 1.2 GHz mid-band post-C-band. Capex $10.5 billion FY2025, 18% of revenue: 40% 5G densification, 30% FTTH, edge for media. "One Network, One Bill" convergence: 25% wireless adds bundle broadband/streaming, blended ARPU up 8%, cross-sell 42%. NexAI cuts SAC 12% to $350, Open RAN trials opex 15%.

Risks: T-Mobile pricing, BEAD delays, enterprise softness. Upside from 6G with Qualcomm. Positions for mid-single-digit growth, EBITDA margins up 100 basis points to 42% on leverage.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the fiber buildout progress, coverage expansion, and customer adoption rates?

Chris Harlan: Certainly, John. As Dana detailed, we added 1.2 million homes passed to reach 18.4 million, with strong regional execution in Southeast, Midwest, and beyond, supported by RDOF and BEAD. Adoption surged with 285,000 net adds to 4.2 million RGUs, take rates at 22.8% overall and over 35% in mature clusters, driven by pricing, bundling, and low 0.85% churn. We're on pace for 25 million passed by YE26, monetizing faster than peers.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Davis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis: Hi, thanks for taking my question. Could you elaborate on your plans for churn rate management heading into next year?

Dana Patel: Yes, Emily. Our Q3 blended churn of 1.12% improved 15 basis points year-over-year, with postpaid wireless at 0.82%, fiber at 1.05%, and streaming at 4.2%. AI prediction and dynamic pricing averted $120 million losses, bundles cut churn 2.5x, and we guide Q4 to 1.05-1.10%. Retention flywheel supports FY25 growth.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Chris, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Chris Harlan: Thank you. In closing, I am proud of our team's performance this quarter. We are well-positioned to continue delivering value to our customers and shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
